A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study despite the revised title and organization. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on corrupted visual instruction tuning, parameter removal, sample identification and performance recovery across multiple models and benchmarks.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, precision-recall curves, parameter-removal experiments and recovery analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, self-validation prompt and subsequent fine-tuning pipeline remain. However, v1 describes lower scores as indicating clean samples, while v2 explicitly selects high Val_PPL scores; v2 Appendix E.2 still retains the lower-score rule. Whether this reflects a procedural change or an incompletely corrected description is unresolved.

E1.justification: The training datasets, eleven evaluation benchmarks, task groups and corruption types remain unchanged. V2's prominent corruption-versus-removal comparison and 20% corruption recovery results already appear in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain GCE, Phuber CE, MentorNet, Co-teaching, JoCoR, EL2N, GradNorm, Entropy and PPL, together with the same clean-data and from-scratch controls. Revised group labels do not introduce different comparators.

E3.justification: The main-text sample-filtering protocol is revised from v1's blanket lower-score-is-clean rule to selecting higher Val_PPL scores in v2 Sections 5.1.1–5.2. This is a reported protocol correction, with the appendix still inconsistent. The retained training sizes, backbones, benchmark metrics and corruption settings otherwise match.

E4.justification: V2 removes the probability-ratio separability analysis in v1 Figure 5 right and the clean-sample probability analysis in Appendix E.4. The standalone ground-truth recovery sweep in v1 Figure 3, including 60% corruption, also disappears. Most recovery, pruning and hyperparameter analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. The different data-loader seeds used for Co-teaching and JoCoR are documented in both versions.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 6–9 retain their numerical results. Some plotted results disappear, notably the probability-ratio traces, the clean-sample conditional-probability curves and ground-truth recovery at 60% corruption. The newly prominent benchmark and 20% recovery plots reuse existing results.

T1.justification: The Bayes-rule derivation and uniform-corruption independence assumption are retained in Appendix E.3. SNIP, perplexity, baseline losses and other score definitions remain mathematically equivalent; relocation and expanded derivation steps do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the headline discrimination claim from corruption improving this ability to corrupted models retaining it. It emphasizes reversible damage rather than superficial damage. The stronger discrimination observation remains in Section 5.1.2, and the principal mitigation contribution is retained.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly links self-validation robustness to an unseen response format and attributes corruption awareness to prior image-text pretraining. It removes v1's detailed competing-objective and ratio-separability explanations. The limitations concerning small models and untested larger models remain.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents selecting the highest 30% of Val_PPL scores, or 30K samples, and clarifies that pretraining data are not corrupted. These disclosures do not establish changed experimental budgets. V1's acknowledgment identifying MindSpore, CANN and Ascend hardware is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wu et al.'s work on triplet-level hallucination evaluation and removes the GPT-4o system-card and Box–Cox references. The broader positioning relative to data enhancement, noisy-label learning and multimodal models remains stable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and much of the main narrative are rewritten. V1's separate defense and experiment sections are reorganized into v2 Section 5, emphasizing retained capabilities; mathematical analysis moves into the appendix. Post-training terminology is widely replaced with further fine-tuning.

P2.justification: V2 splits the opening composite figure, redraws precision-recall results into separately annotated panels, brings existing appendix results into the main text and combines low- and high-corruption recovery plots. Diagnostic panels are removed, and appendix figures and tables are substantially relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity through more precise headline claims, separated precision-recall displays and an explicit sample-selection size, while preserving the principal numerical evidence. The gains are limited by removed supporting probability analyses and the unresolved disagreement between the main-text Val_PPL selection direction and Appendix E.2.
